digest: Here is a quick summary of the recent updates: ACLI Dispatcher worked on 3 updates. Ed worked on 4 updates. The last update was from ACLI Dispatcher, saying: **@claude**: I've read the full plan. Here's my honest review against your specific requirement — **...

Work has shifted from Fable 5 design review to an executable Pool3 implementation plan. Codex created the canonical plan and updated the roadmap, tasks, and project log.

The plan’s core decision is a narrow paper-only walking skeleton: five ETFs, daily data, one strategy, risk gate, internal paper broker, SQLite audit ledger, approval CLI, digest, manifests, and tests. No production code has been built yet.

Claude reviewed the plan and found one key gap: milestones are too large for your desired build, AI-audit, and manual-review rhythm. The proposed fix is to divide the first skeleton into eight small, tangible steps, each ending with a command you can run and inspect yourself.

The immediate next action is still planning, not coding: add a verification protocol and exact manual test commands to the implementation plan. Once you approve that contract, Step 1 is documenting the five-ETF universe and canonical risk policy.

Ed, work is now centered on Pool3’s Fable 5 implementation plan, not the Voice Channel build.

Codex completed the comprehensive plan and made it canonical in the roadmap, task list, and project log. The first target is a narrow paper-only system: five ETFs, daily data, one strategy, risk controls, internal paper broker, audited ledger, approval workflow, digest, and tests.

Claude’s review found the plan is architecturally strong but not yet aligned with your desired build-and-review rhythm. The current milestones are too large for frequent verification.

The recommended fix is an eight-step ladder. Each small step ends with an AI audit and one concrete command you can run and inspect yourself, such as viewing recent bars, checking an as-of query, inspecting a signal, running a backtest, forcing a stale-data rejection, verifying the ledger, and approving a draft.

Nothing is technically blocked. The immediate next action is to add this verification protocol and exact manual test commands to the implementation plan, then have you review that contract before coding begins.
